title: Lump-Sum Settlement Extension Allowance for the Consumer's Payment Track Record
content:
# Lump-Sum Settlement — Track-Record Allowance

The consumer payments posted to a placed account, as its Placed Consumer Accounts money history shows them, form the track record that bears on a due-date extension of an accepted Lump-Sum Settlement under Ridgeline's Settlement Agreements.

**Rule.** Every consumer payment posted to the settled account counts toward the Lump-Sum track record, a payment that was later returned included; where three or more have been posted, the Lump-Sum track-record allowance of 2 days is added; where one or two have been posted, the Lump-Sum track-record allowance is 1 day; an account with no posted consumer payment carries no Lump-Sum track-record allowance.

| Consumer payments posted to the settled account (returned ones included) | Track-record allowance |
|---|---|
| 3 or more | 2 days |
| 1 or 2 | 1 day |
| none | none |

## Basis Q&A

**Q. Two payments were posted and one of them was later returned. How many count?**
A. Two. A payment later returned still counts, so the allowance is 1 day.

**Q. Do the posted payments need to be recent?** No period is set; every consumer payment posted to the settled account counts.

**Q. Three payments posted: is the allowance 3 days?** No. Three or more posted earns 2 days.
